newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ERA sees full yr net profit near last year.
newsitem.headline: ERA sees full yr net profit near last year.

text.p: Uranium miner Energy Resources of Australia Ltd (ERA) said on Wednesday its full year profit for the year to June 30, 1997 should go close to reaching last year's levels.
ERA said its net profit after tax for the first nine months came in at A$20.4 million, compared with A$11.6 million in the previous corresponding period.
Net profit for the March quarter was A$5.2 million, compared with A$0.9 million in the same period last year.

"Given the strong operating performance in the first nine months, and notwithstanding the absence of similar benefits to those received last year in relation to the Division 3B tax case, it is likely that this year's full year profits should go close to reaching last year's levels," ERA said in a statement.
ERA, which is majority owned by North Ltd, posted a net profit of A$40.73 million for the year to June 30, 1996, up from A$12.37 million previously.
ERA last year received a A$3.17 million tax refund after a successful challenge against the Commissioner of Taxation.
The miner said revenue for the March quarter was A$41.2 million, on sales of 1,040.3 tonnes of uranium oxide.
The Ranger mine produced 988.5 tonnes of uranium oxide during the quarter, taking production for the nine months to 2,918.4 tonnes, compared with 2,110.5 tonnes previously.
ERA said it expected about 430 tonnes of extra Ranger material to be released for sale in the fourth quarter, due to a uranium loan negotiated earlier this year.
